b:
Whatever lips may spill,
if it is my sweet Tamil,
my belly is filled,
my blood throbs,
and sometimes
my lips do too

§

"We will reach
a per-capita income of eight thousand dollars"
– the Government
When will he
ever hold
eight thousand dollars?
Yours sincerely,
a thousand-rupee note

§

I am short of breath:
I am
a single fold
of your sari's border
caught
between the fingers
of your tender hands

Reborn,
I have jumped
into the forest of your hair;
now,
pet teasing
with your fingernails

§

I
have run dry

Give me
a few of your
words
as dowry,

so that a poem
can be the groom

§

I want those who come near me with love,
talking literature under a moon of joy
I want to fly like a cloud
I want youth to stay in my body
I want to set foot in every forest and field
and freeze in time
I want to put flowers in a woman's hair;
I want to lean on her breast and sleep
I want talent and strength
I want to hold what I sought
Words, meaning and delicious Tamil:
I want them with me like a shadow, never leaving
And if I cannot have all that I want,
I want Bharathi alone, every day
note: The first scribble is a play on four Tamil words of similar sound: atharam (lip), utharam (belly), uthiram (blood) and uthadu (lip). In the dowry scribble, the poet is the bride's family asking for words as dowry, with the poem as groom. The last echoes Subramania Bharathi's famous poem of wishes, each line ending "vēṇṭum" ("I want").
